explanation: There is no basis for treating the head as the body's 'most sacred and dignified part' tied to Islamic teaching — a well-known hadith actually encourages gently stroking an orphan's head as an act of kindness, so the gesture toward children reads as affectionate. Toward an adult, head-patting is more a matter of overfamiliarity and perceived disrespect than a religious violation.
local_tip: Reserve head-patting for children you know, and offer a handshake or warm word instead with adults.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred part of the body, so touching it, child or adult, is a serious breach of etiquette.
Patting a child's head is often affectionate, but touching an adult's head is generally seen as disrespectful.
Patting a child's head on the head usually reads as friendly, though context still matters with adults.

sources.title: Hadith on Orphans: Be kind to orphans for a soft heart
